data.title: International Gemological Institute achieves MPS as Blackstone sells 1.55% stake to Stallion Asset, Old Bridge MF among seven investors
data.description:
International Gemological Institute, which certifies diamonds, coloured stones and jewellery, achieved the minimum public shareholding (MPS) requirement on November 27 after promoter Blackstone, through its affiliate, offloaded a 1.55 percent stake in the company through open-market transactions.

According to block deal data on Friday, BCP Asia II Topco, an affiliate of Blackstone, sold 67.16 lakh equity shares of International Gemological Institute for Rs 280.05 crore. The transaction represented 1.55 percent of the company's paid-up equity capital.

Seven institutional investors, including Stallion Asset and Old Bridge Mutual Fund, acquired the entire stake sold by Blackstone at Rs 417 per share.

Stallion Asset purchased 11.98 lakh equity shares of International Gemological Institute for Rs 49.97 crore, while Old Bridge Mutual Fund acquired 24 lakh shares for Rs 100.08 crore. Citigroup Global Markets Singapore purchased 7.19 lakh shares for Rs 30 crore.

Additionally, Morgan Stanley Asia Singapore, Susquehanna Pacific, Ashoka India Equity Investment Trust and WhiteOak Capital Mutual Fund each acquired 5.99 lakh shares for Rs 25 crore.

Following the 1.55 percent stake sale, the total shareholding of the promoter and promoter group in International Gemological Institute declined from 76.55 percent to 75 percent of the paid-up equity share capital, while public shareholding increased to 25 percent, the company said in its filing.

Accordingly, the company has achieved the minimum public shareholding requirement.

Shares of International Gemological Institute rose 1.52 percent to close at Rs 429.65 on Friday, after declining 4.8 percent from the day's high.

Aegis Investment Fund buys 0.5% stake in Jagran Prakashan

Meanwhile, Aegis Investment Fund purchased 11 lakh shares of Jagran Prakashan, representing 0.5 percent of its paid-up equity capital, for Rs 7.61 crore.

The shares were purchased at Rs 69.19 apiece.

Jagran Prakashan stock staged a stellar performance on Friday, surging 9.5 percent to Rs 68.26 amid high trading volumes. The stock extended its gains for the third consecutive session.

Tiger Strategies Fund sells shares worth Rs 12 crore in Shalimar Paints

Tiger Strategies Fund-I offloaded 11 lakh shares of Shalimar Paints for Rs 11.88 crore. The shares were sold at Rs 108.01 apiece.

However, Shalimar Paints shares rose 0.43 percent to Rs 108.57, extending their upward trend for the fourth consecutive session. The rally was accompanied by high trading volumes, particularly following a gap-up opening on November 23.

data.title: Verizon in talks to buy Fidium in $6B deal — FT
data.description:
Verizon is in discussions to purchase fibre-optic broadband operator Fidium for about $6 billion.

Talks between Verizon and Fidium’s owners, Searchlight Capital Partners, and Canadian fund manager British Columbia Investment Management Corporation are ongoing, according to a Financial Times report on Friday, which cited people familiar with the matter. A potential $6 billion deal, which includes debt, could happen in the coming weeks.

It's possible that another bidder could emerge, and there are no guarantees the talks will result in a transaction, according to the report. Searchlight and BCI bought Fidium, then known as Consolidated Communications, in a $3.1 billion take-private deal in 2024.

Verizon and Searchlight declined to comment to the FT. BCI and Fidium did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

data.title: SBI To Recruit 1,540 Junior Associates Under Special Drive
data.description:
The bank is filling reserved-category backlog vacancies as part of a broader plan to onboard 11,000–12,000 employees in FY27

State Bank of India (SBI) has announced the recruitment of 1,540 Junior Associates (Customer Support and Sales) through a special drive to fill backlog vacancies in reserved categories across states and Union Territories.

The recruitment is aimed at strengthening workforce representation and expanding the bank's customer-facing capabilities, while addressing vacancies that have remained unfilled in the reserved categories.

The selection process comprised a preliminary examination held on September 16, 2026, followed by the main examination on October 29. SBI has published the provisional selection results, with appointments subject to fulfilment of eligibility conditions and local language proficiency requirements.

Commenting on the initiative, SBI Chairman Challa Sreenivasulu Setty said the special recruitment drive was undertaken in line with the Government of India's directions to fill backlog vacancies within a stipulated timeframe. He added that the initiative reflected the bank's commitment to social inclusion, equal opportunity and greater workforce representation.

The recruitment is part of SBI's broader workforce expansion plans for FY27. The bank intends to onboard approximately 11,000–12,000 employees across clerical and officer cadres during the financial year, taking into account retirements and emerging business requirements.

SBI also plans to expand its branch network by approximately 200–250 branches during FY27. The additional workforce is expected to support the expansion, strengthen branch operations and improve customer service delivery.

With a workforce of around 2.47 lakh employees, SBI remains one of India's largest employers. Its recruitment plans reflect the continuing demand for frontline banking personnel even as the sector increasingly adopts digital platforms and technology-led services.

data.title: Gail, GNFC Explore Joint Investments In Downstream Petrochemicals
data.description:
The companies have signed an MoU to assess potential investments, bringing together Gail’s petrochemical infrastructure and GNFC’s chemicals manufacturing capabilities

Gail (India) and Gujarat Narmada Valley Fertilisers & Chemicals (GNFC) have signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) to jointly explore the feasibility of developing downstream petrochemical projects, as the two state-owned companies look to identify new business opportunities in the sector.

The agreement, signed in New Delhi on 27 November, will allow the companies to assess potential projects by leveraging their existing infrastructure, manufacturing capabilities and industry experience.

The proposed collaboration is aimed at expanding opportunities in India's downstream petrochemical segment and strengthening the domestic petrochemical value chain. However, the companies have not disclosed specific projects, investment commitments, production capacities or implementation timelines.

Focus On Downstream Expansion

The collaboration will bring together Gail's presence across the natural gas and petrochemical value chain with GNFC's experience in fertilisers and industrial chemicals.

Gail plans to leverage its existing infrastructure to examine opportunities in downstream petrochemicals, which involve converting basic petrochemical feedstocks into higher-value products used across industrial and consumer sectors.

The segment supplies raw materials to industries such as automobiles, textiles, packaging and construction, among others. Expanding domestic downstream manufacturing can also create opportunities for greater value addition within the country's petrochemical industry.

Senior Executives Sign Agreement

The MoU was signed by Sanjay Agarwal, Executive Director (Business Development, Start-up and Research & Development) at GailL, and D.V. Parikh, Executive Director and Chief Financial Officer of GNFC. R.K. Singhal, Director (Business Development) at Gail, was present at the signing.

Singhal said the agreement would support efforts to strengthen India's petrochemical value chain, with Gail looking to utilise its existing infrastructure to explore the development of downstream projects.

Parikh said the partnership could open new avenues for both companies in the downstream petrochemicals sector.

data.title: Sebi Extends Tata Steel’s APL Apollo Open Offer Disclosure Deadline To 8 December
data.description:
The seven-day extension applies to the detailed public statement, while the deadline for filing the draft letter of offer remains unchanged

The Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) has given Tata Steel an additional seven days to publish the detailed public statement for its proposed open offer to acquire up to 26 per cent of APL Apollo Tubes, extending the deadline to 8 December 2026.

The extension follows a request from Tata Steel, with Kotak Mahindra Capital Company, the manager to the open offer, informing stock exchanges about the regulator's decision through a filing on Friday.

Under the revised timeline, Tata Steel can publish the detailed public statement by 8 December instead of the earlier deadline of 1 December. However, the deadline for submitting the draft letter of offer to Sebi remains 8 December, the filing clarified.

The extension comes amid scrutiny of the proposed Tata Steel-APL Apollo transaction, particularly over its potential implications for minority shareholders.

Sebi Chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey on Friday said the regulator considers minority shareholders' interests important, responding to questions about concerns surrounding the transaction.

Deal Involves Rs 32,266 Cr

Tata Steel announced the proposed acquisition earlier this week, targeting a maximum 52.38 per cent stake in APL Apollo Tubes through a combination of a promoter stake purchase and a mandatory open offer.

The company will acquire a 26.38 per cent stake from APL Apollo's promoter group for approximately Rs 15,510.61 crore. It will separately make an open offer to public shareholders to acquire up to an additional 26 per cent stake for approximately Rs 16,755.66 crore.

The open offer, announced on 23 November, covers up to 7,28,06,387 equity shares of APL Apollo Tubes. The combined transaction is valued at approximately Rs 32,266 crore.

Business Transfer Adds To Consolidation

Separately, Tata Steel will transfer its steel tubes and colour-coated businesses to APL Apollo for a combined consideration of Rs 28,000 crore.

The proposed consolidation is expected to initially increase the combined manufacturing capacity for tubes and colour-coated products to 7.5 million tonne per annum. The companies are targeting a capacity of 15.5 million tonne by 2035.

The acquisition and business transfer would expand APL Apollo's manufacturing scale while allowing Tata Steel to consolidate its downstream steel products operations through the proposed arrangement.

data.title: 8th Pay Commission May Add Rs 3 Lakh Cr To Centre's Expenditure: Deutsche Bank
data.description:
8th Pay Commission's estimated cost could complicate fiscal consolidation even as higher salaries may support consumption; bank sees fiscal deficit at 4.3 per cent of GDP in FY28

The implementation of the 8th Pay Commission could add at least Rs 3 lakh crore to the Centre's expenditure, making it harder for the government to meet its fiscal consolidation targets in 2027-28, according to Deutsche Bank Research.

In its 2027 World Outlook report, titled Great Expectations, but Risky Business, the bank said the additional financial burden from the pay revision, alongside elevated crude oil prices, rising subsidy requirements and potentially lower dividend receipts from the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), could put pressure on government finances.

Deutsche Bank expects the Centre's fiscal deficit to remain at 4.3 per cent of gross domestic product (GDP) in FY28, the same level projected for the current financial year.

The estimated cost of implementing the 8th Pay Commission recommendations is marginally higher than the Rs 2.9 lakh crore dividend transfer from the RBI that the bank expects the government to receive in FY27. However, the two estimates relate to different financial years and do not imply that the central bank's dividend would directly fund the pay revision.

The bank said postponing the implementation of the pay commission recommendations until 2028 could offer some temporary relief to government finances. However, the delay could also result in a larger accumulation of arrears, increasing the eventual payout.

Deutsche Bank expects the Centre to implement the pay commission awards from next year, which could provide an additional boost to household incomes and domestic consumption.

For FY27, the bank expects the government to meet its fiscal deficit target of 4.3 per cent of GDP, supported by higher-than-expected RBI dividend receipts, a provision of Rs 1 lakh crore under the Economic Stabilisation Fund, a possible reduction in capital expenditure and stronger disinvestment proceeds.

The expected RBI dividend transfer of Rs 2.9 lakh crore is among the factors supporting the government's fiscal position in the current financial year. However, the bank cautioned that the fiscal arithmetic could become more demanding in FY28 as the expenditure implications of the 8th Pay Commission begin to emerge.

The potential increase in salaries and wages could, nevertheless, support economic activity by improving disposable incomes among central government employees and stimulating consumption.

Deutsche Bank projected India's real GDP growth at 7.3 per cent in FY27, 7.2 per cent in FY28 and 7.3 per cent in FY29.

The bank said the Indian economy had demonstrated resilience despite the ongoing West Asia crisis and a below-normal monsoon, although external risks and fiscal pressures remain relevant to the growth outlook.

The projections come ahead of the Union Budget for 2027-28, when the government will have to balance additional spending commitments, including the implementation of the 8th Pay Commission, with its efforts to bring down the fiscal deficit.

The pay commission's recommendations are expected to cover salary and pension revisions for central government employees and pensioners, potentially creating a substantial recurring expenditure commitment for the Centre.

data.title: Adani Group Seeks Govt Nod To Invest In Airline Business
data.description:
Adani Group seeks government permission to fund existing airlines or back new entrants, citing India's untapped aviation demand and the need to expand daily flight operations

Adani Group wants to enter India's airline business and has asked the government to permit it to invest in existing carriers or back entrepreneurs seeking to establish new airlines, Group Chief Financial Officer Jugeshinder (Robbie) Singh said on Friday.

Speaking on the sidelines of the India Debt Capital Market Summit in Mumbai, Singh said India had considerable untapped demand for air travel, with an estimated 600 million potential passengers yet to be served adequately by the country's aviation network.

He said India currently operates around 3,200-3,300 flights daily, a number that would need to increase nearly tenfold to 30,000 to meet the country's potential demand.

The comments mark the clearest public indication yet from a senior group-level executive that Adani Group is exploring an entry into the airline business, extending its aviation interests beyond airport infrastructure.

Singh said the conglomerate wants the government to create an avenue for it to participate in the sector, either by providing capital to an existing airline or supporting an entrepreneur willing to launch a new carrier. Such investments, he said, could accelerate the expansion of airline capacity and improve connectivity for millions of Indians who currently lack access to suitable flight routes.

He said the group's interest in aviation was driven by the opportunity to serve this largely untapped passenger base, rather than concerns surrounding its airport projects in Mumbai and Navi Mumbai.

Singh said the development of airport infrastructure would need to be accompanied by a corresponding expansion in airline operations. While the group has invested in building airport capacity, airlines would have to increase their fleets, operations and route networks to ensure that the infrastructure is fully utilised.

Adani Group's proposed participation in the airline sector could therefore take the form of financial backing rather than necessarily setting up and operating an airline itself, Singh indicated.

The group has not disclosed the potential size of its investment, identified any prospective airline partners or provided a timeline for its proposed entry into the sector.

data.title: ATEX Stock Jumps After SpaceX Reportedly Eyes 900 MHz Spectrum For Direct-To-Device Expansion; Alternative Target NN Climbs Double Digits
data.description:
Key points:
  • According to Guttman-McCabe, who noted that the company could hand off its remaining licenses to a single party, the company’s remaining spectrum could triple in value with the right buyer. 
  • SpaceX is trying to put together its own retail wireless network and compete with big mobile network operators like Verizon, T-Mobile US, and AT&T Mobility.
  • SpaceX CEO Elon Musk has previously said that his company would take only “2 or 3 years to build a full terrestrial network.

Shares of Anterix Inc. (ATEX) jumped on Friday after a report that Elon Musk’s SpaceX (SPCX) is eyeing an acquisition of the New Jersey company’s 900 MHz licenses to support expansion of its direct-to-device satellite service.

ATEX stock was up 9% at the time of writing, while SPCX shares traded up 4%. Shares of NextNav (NN), another 900 MHz license holder, rose 12%.

Why Is Anterix Looking To Sell?

Anterix has historically leased spectrum to utilities for grid modernization but has opened the door to bigger outright spectrum sales and recurring revenue-generating services, Bloomberg noted. Only about 15% of its holdings are currently used by a handful of utilities, leaving 85% available.

Chris Guttman-McCabe, Anterix’s head of corporate development, told Bloomberg that the company is talking to “all the right parties.” “We’re talking to anyone who can help us drive shareholder value,” he said.

According to Guttman-McCabe, who noted that the company could hand off its remaining licenses to a single party, the company’s remaining spectrum could triple in value with the right buyer.

“Licensed low-band spectrum is hardest to come by, and we have it,” Anterix CEO Scott Lang said on the company’s last earnings call.

Why Is SpaceX Interested in ATEX?

SpaceX, meanwhile, is trying to put together its own retail wireless network and compete with big mobile network operators like Verizon (VZ), T-Mobile US (TMUS), and AT&T Mobility (T). The company previously acquired a significant tranche of spectrum from EchoStar Corp. in 2025 and 800 MHz licenses from Grain Management in October.

VZ and T shares rose around 1% each in afternoon trade. TMUS stock was up around 2%. Retail sentiment across the three telecommunication companies varied, with sentiment in the ‘bullish’ zone for T-Mobile US, in the ‘neutral’ zone for Verizon and in the ‘bearish’ zone for AT&T, over the past day.

Last month, Bloomberg also reported that SpaceX is pursuing agreements for a minimum of 80,000 cell sites across the United States as it advances plans to build a fourth nationwide wireless carrier. The report said that SpaceX is in discussions with at least one major cellular infrastructure company and that Crown Castle Inc. (CCI), among the largest U.S. owners of cellular towers alongside American Tower (AMT) and Vertical Bridge, was also approached for the purpose.

However, late last month, Verizon CEO Dan Schulman dismissed the near-term threat from SpaceX’s network-building ambitions, arguing that any serious challenge in the U.S. mobile market would require a full terrestrial network costing hundreds of billions of dollars and taking four to six years to build. SpaceX CEO Elon Musk disputed the timeline, saying that his company would take only “2 or 3 years.”

Bloomberg noted that the FCC decisions on awarding satellite designation to Anterix’s spectrum could curb its usefulness for the direct-to-device market that SpaceX is trying to scale. Further, SpaceX could also instead buy geolocation service provider NextNav’s 900 MHz airwaves.

How Did ATEX, NN, SPCX Retail Traders React?

On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around SPCX and ATEX was trending in ‘bullish’ territory over the past day. Sentiment around NN, meanwhile, stayed within ‘bearish’ levels.

While ATEX stock has soared 275% year-to-date, NN shares have fallen 45%. SPCX, meanwhile, is currently trading at around $131, below its June IPO price of $135.

data.title: Saudi Insurance Industry Could See Further Consolidation Under New Capital Rules — Market Talk
data.description: Saudi Arabia's new capital framework could drive further consolidation in the kingdom's insurance industry, Bahrain-based investment bank SICO says. The framework, effective from 2027, will link insurers' capital requirements to risks associated with their policies and investments. The Saudi Insurance Authority aims to double industry capital to 50 billion riyals by 2030. Smaller insurers with limited capital and weak earnings could need to raise equity, issue subordinated debt or be acquired. Bupa Arabia and Tawuniya, which together accounted for around 82% of first-half sector pretax profit, stand to benefit, SICO says. (farhan.rafid@wsj.com)

data.title: Tethys Petroleum Press Release (TPL): Interim Results and Corporate Update
data.description:
Grand Cayman, Cayman Islands--(Newsfile Corp. - November 27, 2026) - Tethys Petroleum Limited ("Tethys" or the "Company") today announced that it has filed its interim results for the three months ended September 30, 2026 with the Canadian securities regulatory authorities comprising its Unaudited Financial Statements together with Management's Discussion and Analysis and other required forms. Copies of the filed documents may be obtained via SEDAR at www.sedarplus.ca or on Tethys' website at www.tethys-group.com.

Financial highlights

Oil and gas sales increased by 130% to $16.3 million in the third quarter of 2026 from $7.1 million in 2025 due to increased oil production and commencing processing crude oil into refined products during the quarter. The net profit for the quarter was $.4 million compared with the net profit of $1.4 million in 2025. Profit after tax for the nine-month period was $2.4 million compared with $2.9 million in 2025. This decrease in profit is primarily attributable to lower oil prices. Total oil and gas production for the period was up 32% as compared to 2025. This increased revenue, but profitability was adversely affected by the additional refining, transportation and excise costs associated with increased production volumes, new operating model, higher oil production costs and increased administrative expenses, particularly professional fees.

Average oil production now is approximately 555 tons per day (4,440 bopd).

Cancellation of Auction

The auction for the sale of the TAG pipeline assets commenced as scheduled at 10:00 a.m. local time in Aktobe on November 26th but was interrupted following a technical issue with the electronic auction platform.

The Company has subsequently received formal notification from the electronic auction platform confirming that the auction lot has been cancelled by the organizer due to a database failure on the platform.

Suspension of Enforcement Proceeding

Separately, on November 26, 2026, the private bailiff issued a formal order suspending the enforcement proceedings against TAG, citing the Administrative Court's request for the enforcement case file pursuant to its ruling of November 25, 2026.

The bailiff's order took effect on the date of its issuance. The administrative proceedings remain ongoing, with a preliminary hearing scheduled for December 7, 2026.

The Company continues to pursue its legal remedies and reserves all its rights in relation to the enforcement proceedings and the auction.

Potential Operational Impact

As previously disclosed, the pledged gas pipelines and related infrastructure are used in TAG's gas production and transportation operations, and any future sale to a third party or transfer of the assets to Special Financial Company DSFK LLP, the holder of the security over TAG's assets, could affect TAG's continued access to and use of this infrastructure. Tethys continues to evaluate legal and commercial measures to protect its interests and maintain continuity of operations.

The Company will provide a further update when additional information becomes available.

About Tethys

Tethys is focused on oil and gas exploration and production activities in Central Asia and the Caspian Region. Tethys believes that significant potential exists in both exploration and in discovered deposits in the area.

data.title: Canada Pumps Billions More For Battered Forest Industry
data.description:
By Paul Vieira

OTTAWA--Canada unveiled on Friday a multibillion-dollar plan to reverse the dwindling fortunes of the country's forest-products sector, which is struggling under the weight of U.S. tariffs and faces acute risks unless addressed.

Canada's Natural Resources Minister Tim Hodgson said the task at hand is to revitalize the sector and stop the flight of capital to the U.S. and elsewhere. Alongside hefty tariffs, Canadian officials acknowledged some of the forestry sector's challenges are homegrown, among them chronic underinvestment and regulatory overlap that thwarts access to cost-competitive fiber used in the production of pulp and paper.

For Hodgson's efforts, Canada has allocated an additional 6.5 billion Canadian dollars (US$4.5 billion) for forestry-sector improvements, building on C$3 billion provided in August 2025 to help with the fallout from U.S. tariffs. All told, the Canadian government has made available roughly C$33 billion in financing for all trade-exposed companies, and about C$10 billion in direct support for affected workers.

Most Canadian exports of softwood lumber - used in the construction of houses - face U.S. duties and tariffs of nearly 35%. Ottawa and Washington have engaged in a decades-long row about lumber products, with U.S. officials accusing Canada of unfairly subsidizing its forest industry.

Officials added forest-product exports have dropped 22% since President Trump imposed further duties on the sector. This has led to the closure of 12 Canadian sawmills, and output curtails in 40 other plants, the officials added.

Hodgson said the government wants to improve access to fibre, accelerate innovation in the sector, and drive domestic demand for Canadian forest products. "Business as usual is no longer an option for our forest sector," he said, adding the government's plan is meant to help the sector navigate current challenges and secure its future.

The additional money for Canada's forest sector is in response to findings from a government-appointed task force, which this year warned the industry faces an existential risk. "Continued inaction will accelerate capital flight, erode skilled workforces, destabilize rural and Indigenous communities, and forgo a generational opportunity to position Canada as a leader in the emerging global bioeconomy," the task force said.

Canada is home to nearly 10% of the world's forests, and about 40% of the country is covered by timberland. But the sector's economic heft has weakened considerably over the decades. Government data indicate that forest products account for about 1% of Canada's gross domestic product, down from a 3% level over two decades ago. Meanwhile, employment in the sector is about 40% below 2004 levels, and softwood-lumber production has declined by nearly a third from 2017 levels.

Of the C$6.5 billion made available, officials said about one-quarter of that cash will be focused on improving productivity at existing sawmills, while the remaining monies are expected to invest in new large-scale factories to accelerate the development of advanced forest products.

Write to Paul Vieira at paul.vieira@wsj.com

data.title: ADBE Stock On Track For 4-Day Rally: Adobe Reports Surge In AI Traffic, $7.1B Thanksgiving Sales
data.description:
Key points:
  • Adobe projects AI-driven retail traffic will rise 130% overall this holiday season and 95% on Black Friday.
  • AI-referred shoppers are generating 83% higher revenue per visit and converting at a 90% higher rate this holiday season, Adobe said.
  • Cyber Monday is projected to be the first single day to eclipse $15 billion in U.S. online spending.

U.S. shoppers are increasingly leaning on AI tools to compare models, evaluate specifications, and weigh alternatives before visiting a retailer's website or store, according to Adobe's 2026 holiday shopping data.

According to Adobe’s holiday sales trends report for 2026, stronger digital demand is propelling overall e-commerce growth this season. Marta Frattini, the global retail and consumer strategy lead at Adode, said in a LinkedIn post that the company projects online Black Friday sales will reach $12.9 billion, up 9.2% from a year earlier, followed by an expected $15.1 billion on Cyber Monday—a projected single-day record spend as per Adobe.

Thanksgiving sales alone came in at $7.1 billion, Adobe said. ADBE stock gained about 1% on Friday and is set to end its fourth consecutive session higher.

Value Shoppers Are Relying On AI 

Adobe also forecast AI-referred traffic to U.S. retail sites will climb 130% year over year (YoY) across the holiday season, including a 159% jump on Thanksgiving and a 95% rise on Black Friday.

Separate findings cited within the report showed AI-referred visitors generated 83% more revenue per visit and converted 90% better than other traffic, while 69% of shoppers say they are less likely to return an item bought with help from an AI assistant.

AI-driven traffic to retail sites grew 127% YoY in August 2026 and is projected to remain strong through the holidays, with traffic expected to grow 130% YoY overall and 159% YoY on Thanksgiving as per Adobe.

Consumers are stretching their budgets across both gifts and everyday necessities, using AI to scout for holiday discounts to save on basics such as clothing staples, personal hygiene items, and household cleaning supplies alongside electronics, toys, and apparel.

Electronics are expected to dominate 2026 holiday sales, bringing in $63.3 billion in sales this year’s holiday season followed by apparel.

ADBE Stock: Retail View 

Retail sentiment on Stocktwits around Adobe rose to ‘neutral’ from ‘bearish’ territory over the past day, with ‘normal’ levels of message volume around the stock.

ADBE stock has lost about 33% year-to-date.

data.title: Advantage Energy holder to vote against sale to Canadian Natural Resources
data.description:
Andvantage Energy holder LetkoBrosseau said it plans to vote against its  sale to Canadian Natural Resources and urges fellow holders to reject the offer.

LetkoBrosseau, which has a 5.5% stake in Advantage Energy , is against the deal, as it “significantly undervalues” the company's "high-quality" asset base and long-term potential, according to a statement on Friday.

"CNQ's proposal represents highly opportunistic timing designed to acquire premier, long-life assets at the bottom of the natural gas cycle and during a period of leadership transition," LetkoBrosseau said in the statement. "But given Advantage's leading asset base and strong financial position, it should feel no pressure to pursue a deal now. In fact, when further considering the industry's accelerating M&A environment, the company actually possesses an enviable negotiating position; it is thus weakly playing what is in reality a very good hand."

The comments come after Canadian Natural last Monday said it agreed to acquire Advantage Energy () for ~C$2.53 (US$1.77B), including debt, bolstering the company's position in western Canada. Canadian Natural said it will pay C$13.55/share for Advantage , a nearly 20% premium.

data.title: Saudi Banks Face Funding Pressure as Government Deposits Decline — Market Talk
data.description: Saudi banks face funding pressure as lending expansion continues to outpace deposit growth, Riyadh-based investment firm Riyad Capital says. The private-sector loan-to-deposit ratio rose to 108% in September from 104.3% in June. Private-sector credit grew 6.0% on year in September, compared with customer deposit growth of 4.8%. Government institutions withdrew 59 billion riyals ($15.7 billion) from commercial-bank deposits between July and September. Customers have also continued shifting funds toward interest-bearing time and savings deposits. Meanwhile, the Saudi central bank's official foreign reserves fell by 108 billion riyals to 1.746 trillion riyals during the third quarter. (farhan.rafid@wsj.com)
